cluster_summary: This cluster covers injection vulnerabilities (JDBC parameter injection, JNDI scheme injection, SQL injection) caused by incomplete blacklists, missing scheme or prefix validation, or direct string concatenation of user input into sensitive constructs. The majority of issues stem from assuming user-controlled data is safe when building JDBC URLs or SQL queries without proper validation, canonicalization, or parameterization.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled URLs or server-controlled redirect responses into HTTP clients that automatically follow redirects or reuse a previously validated URL decision. Report code paths where the final redirected scheme, host, port, and resolved address are not revalidated before the sensitive network request. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should disable automatic redirects or revalidate every redirect hop against the same allowlist and address policy.

mechanism.missing_guard: the final redirected scheme, host, port, and resolved address are not revalidated before the sensitive network request
mechanism.name: SSRF through redirect-following client
mechanism.sink_shape: HTTP clients that automatically follow redirects or reuse a previously validated URL decision
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled URLs or server-controlled redirect responses
mechanism.typical_fix: disable automatic redirects or revalidate every redirect hop against the same allowlist and address policy

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Expand the blacklist to cover all known dangerous parameters and protocols, apply the check after full URL assembly and URL-decoding, and use robust regex that matches parameter names regardless of context.
sub_patterns.name: Incomplete or misapplied blacklist for JDBC connection parameters
sub_patterns.root_cause: The application relies on a blacklist to filter dangerous JDBC URL parameters, but the blacklist is missing entries (e.g., socketFactory, autoDeserialize, iiop), applied too early (before URL assembly or decoding), or uses overly restrictive regex patterns, allowing bypass.
